Packing must receive valid tokens as a contiguous prefix: compact each left-padded history into chronological, right-padded form before `pack_padded_sequence`; verify lengths, sorting/restoration, and alignment back to original positions. In the original left-padded layout, read the final nonpadding position, never `count-1`; that index applies only after compaction. Handle empty histories explicitly with the same defined fallback in both paths—packing requires positive lengths; clamping zero to one introduces a synthetic recurrent step. Check empty, singleton, mixed-length and maximum-length cases. [Packing documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html), [implementation](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/PackedSequence.cpp).

PyTorch distinguishes per-timestep last-layer GRU outputs from final recurrent hidden states. For a unidirectional packed GRU, compare the last valid raw output with the corresponding top-layer `h_n`, preserving batch order and initial states. A projected, normalized, activated or residual-enhanced `log2feats` output must be compared against an identically transformed hidden state. Diagnostic inference: when aligned sequence features pass but final features fail, first extract both readouts from the same forward result; inspect indices, empty-row policy, transformations and comparison semantics before attributing failure to a readout bug. [GRU documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html).

Use identical weights, inputs, evaluation mode, dtype and initial states. Compare repeated identical-shape runs, then singleton versus mixed-batch runs; isolate recurrence from subsequent transformations. PyTorch explicitly does not guarantee bitwise equality between batched and sliced computations. Test cuDNN-disabled and CPU/float64 references as diagnostic controls; record absolute/relative errors and score/rank effects. Batch-shape differences are a hypothesis requiring evidence, not permission to relax the existing tolerance or dismiss a failed check. [Numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html).
